summary: Fixed test-file bug in /app/backend/tests/test_seismic_map.py where 5 TestDedup tests errored with 'sync test requested async fixture'. Root cause: pytest-asyncio 1.4.0 strict mode requires (1) async fixtures to use @pytest_asyncio.fixture (not @pytest.fixture) and (2) reliable per-method @pytest.mark.asyncio markers rather than class-level marker. All 21/21 tests now pass. No production code touched. Cleanup verified — 0 TEST_MAP_ rows remaining in emsc_events collection after suite completion.

Class-level @pytest.mark.asyncio marker was replaced with per-method markers for reliability in strict mode.

rca_of_issue: Reproduction: pytest backend/tests/test_seismic_map.py → 5 ERRORs at setup of TestDedup.* with message 'requested an async fixture mongo, with no plugin or hook that handled it'. RCA: (a) The `mongo` fixture was declared with @pytest.fixture but is an async generator; under pytest-asyncio strict mode (v1.4.0), async fixtures must be declared via @pytest_asyncio.fixture, otherwise pytest sees it as a regular (sync) fixture that returns an async generator and refuses to inject it into sync tests. (b) The class-level @pytest.mark.asyncio marker on TestDedup was not being propagated to individual methods in strict mode, so pytest-asyncio treated the methods as sync. Mitigation applied: added `import pytest_asyncio`, changed `@pytest.fixture` → `@pytest_asyncio.fixture` on the mongo fixture, and added explicit `@pytest.mark.asyncio` on each of the 5 TestDedup async methods. Result: 21/21 pass in 1.57s; TEST_MAP_ cleanup verified.
